currentContext.strengths: Seqrite Labs, described as India's largest malware analysis facility, draws telemetry from over 8 million endpoints and recorded more than 265 million threat detections during the year, feeding detection intelligence into every product built on it|GoDeep.AI acts as a single shared behavioural-detection intelligence layer across endpoints, networks and data environments, removing the need to run disparate detection engines|Patent portfolio reached nine after two new Indian patents were granted during the year; patents cover signatureless behaviour-based detection, anti-ransomware and zero-trust access control|Nearly three decades of R&D focused on computer and network security, with solutions indigenously developed in India|Independent validation and institutional standing — collaboration with the NIST National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence on its Data Classification project, the AV-TEST Best Performance 2024 Award for Corporate Users for Seqrite Endpoint Protection, and recognition as a Gartner Preferred Vendor|Service reach — 23 offices across 22 cities in India plus offices in the USA and UAE, supporting customers in more than 70 countries with over 900 cybersecurity professionals|Certified operating base: ISO 9001:2015, ISO 20000-1:2018, ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type 2|Partnership with the BHASHINI platform delivering AI capabilities in 22 languages, and with Terrabyte extending reach across Southeast Asia
currentContext.strategies: Strengthen the enterprise cybersecurity business, winning and executing large, integrated cybersecurity engagements across enterprises, government organisations and critical sectors|Expand the international footprint, with continued investment in Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Africa and Latin America to build global presence and new partner ecosystems|Advance innovation across the cybersecurity portfolio, embedding AI to improve the speed, accuracy and effectiveness of threat detection and response through platforms such as GoDeep.AI and the Seqrite Intelligent Assistant|Capitalise on emerging opportunities in data privacy, compliance and digital trust, which management views as a long-term structural opportunity and an important growth area|Evolve the consumer business beyond conventional antivirus into a broader digital safety and digital trust proposition covering fraud, identity theft, phishing and social engineering|Leverage the extensive distribution network, partner ecosystem and brand to deepen consumer engagement and defend consumer market position|Build a future-ready organisation by consolidating key customer-facing and internal platforms into a unified ecosystem using automation and AI for faster, better-informed decision-making|Attract, develop and retain talent across research, engineering, product development, sales and customer-facing functions|Maintain operational discipline, customer success and long-term value creation rather than optimising for a single year's financial outcome|Support cyber-skilling through Quick Heal Academy, aimed at students, working professionals and corporate teams
currentContext.expansion: Expansion during the year was capability-, footprint- and platform-led rather than plant-based; the report discloses no manufacturing capacity. Internationally, the company expanded its global footprint across SEA, MEA and LATAM, with a strategic partnership with Terrabyte extending reach across Southeast Asia and continued investment in Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Latin America supporting longer-term expansion. The enterprise portfolio was widened with newly launched Seqrite DRPS, Seqrite RRaaS and the AntiFraud.AI freemium version, while a partnership with the BHASHINI platform added AI capabilities in 22 languages and the Seqrite Data Privacy Management Platform secured its first enterprise customer. Institutional build-out included advanced cybersecurity laboratories being established with BIRD and NABARD to build cyber capabilities across rural and financial institutions. Internally, sales CRM, customer support, marketing automation and previously siloed IT applications were integrated into a unified digital ecosystem, new leadership was added across Engineering, People & Culture, Marketing, Delivery & Services and Channel & Alliances, and investment in R&D was deepened; a unified partner platform combining CRM, deal registration and customer support, plus structured credit cycles across the distribution network, was rolled out to the channel. On facilities, the R&D centre at Thube Park, Shivaji Nagar, Pune generated 6.81% of its total power requirement from a 45 kW solar plant, the seventh consecutive year of renewable generation there, and the Head Office and R&D centre in Pune and the Nashik office benefit from lower electricity tariffs and electricity duty exemptions under the Maharashtra IT Policy.

risks.risk: AI is eroding the moats and pricing power of software businesses
risks.note: The report itself states that competitive moats long regarded as unassailable — proprietary data and embedded workflows — are facing serious scrutiny, that large language models threaten to strip distinct pricing power from specific software capabilities, and that AI interfaces are increasingly acting as a middle layer between applications and end users. For a proprietary security-software vendor this is a direct threat to the durability of product differentiation and price.

risks.risk: AI-enabled attackers and the detection arms race
risks.note: Malicious actors are aggressively leveraging AI to execute cyberattacks, automating reconnaissance, enhancing deception and establishing persistence — the 'cognitive intrusions' era. Traditional signature-reliant technologies struggle with novel or rapidly mutating techniques, so the detection stack must be continuously re-engineered towards predictive, autonomous and intelligence-led defence or lose relevance.

risks.risk: Adversarial machine learning against the company's own AI models
risks.note: The report enumerates evasion attacks, data poisoning, privacy attacks and white-box attacks as novel challenges arising from the complexity and expansive attack surface of machine-learning models. Since detection is anchored on GoDeep.AI, a compromise or degradation of the models is a risk to the core product, not a peripheral IT issue.

risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance change across data privacy and AI
risks.note: GDPR and India's DPDP Act are described as establishing strict new compliance baselines, with the Digital India Act aiming to consolidate frameworks around cybersecurity prosecution, platform accountability and AI regulation, and the EU AI Act contrasted with a relaxed US approach. Product architecture and privacy capabilities must keep pace with shifting mandates in every market served.

risks.risk: Rising employee attrition in a skills-scarce business
risks.note: The turnover rate for permanent employees rose to 26.00 in FY 2025-26 from 14.63 in FY 2024-25 and 18.07 in FY 2023-24. In a business whose output is research and engineering, and where the report separately flags a critical cybersecurity skills gap, sustained attrition at this level is a structural constraint on delivery and innovation.

Customer complaints in FY 2025-26 numbered 2,56,569, with 14 issues pending at the close of the year — 4 resolved and under observation, 3 with a work-around offered, 4 awaiting an ETA and 3 scheduled to be fixed by Q1. Grievance redressal for customers and value-chain partners runs through the Vulnerability Disclosure Policy, which places product-security defects in the same channel as ordinary support.

risks.risk: Deteriorating profitability and a swing into loss
risks.note: The Board's Report for FY 2025-26 records revenue from operations below the prior year, total expenditure exceeding total income and a loss before and after tax against a profit in the preceding year. The Board states that no risks in its opinion threaten the existence of the Company and that risks of concern are explained in the MD&A, with the Board and Audit Committee updated quarterly and the Risk Management Committee chaired by an Independent Director.

risks.risk: Cybersecurity procurement widening to supply-chain origin and digital sovereignty
risks.note: The Chairman notes that in March 2026 the Government of India introduced a requirement for CCTV cameras deployed in government buildings to disclose the origin of their microchips, reflecting a shift in which cybersecurity extends beyond software protection to supply chains, hardware integrity, digital sovereignty and critical-infrastructure resilience. Procurement rules tied to technology origin can reshape which vendors qualify for government and critical-infrastructure business.

one-line thesis: Quick Heal is strategically pivoting from a declining consumer antivirus business to a high-growth enterprise cybersecurity player, leveraging its dominant SMB market share and new products in EDR/XDR and data privacy; despite near-term revenue pressure, strong margins, zero debt, and NIST validation position it for long-term market capture.
financial scorecard: rev: -52% YoY (Q4); EBITDA: Negative; PAT: Negative; orderbook: Not disclosed; netdebt: Zero
guidance: Revenue to recover in Q2FY24; enterprise segment to reach 50%+ of total revenue within 4-6 quarters; R&D spend targeted at 25-30% of revenue; no explicit revenue or EBITDA guidance provided.
order book & pipeline: Not disclosed; enterprise segment delivered over ₹100cr revenue in FY23 with 20% CAGR over 3 years; 20+ new customers onboarded for EDR/XDR products.
segment / subsidiary detail: Enterprise: ₹93cr+ revenue in FY23 (1/3 of total); 20-25% market share in SMB endpoint security; targeting mid-size enterprises (500-1500 endpoints); 90%+ revenue from Endpoint Protection; new products: EDR, XDR, HawkkScan (data privacy); Consumer: 2/3 of revenue; experiencing temporary decline due to macroeconomic slowdown and delayed renewals; ARPU increasing in both segments.
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into mid-size enterprises and government (B2G); international visibility via NIST collaboration; monetization of data privacy products; potential to capture 5-6x addressable market by combining SMB and mid-enterprise segments.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margins: >95% (unchanged YoY); total expenditure reduced by ₹12cr QoQ; R&D spend to be maintained at 25-30% of revenue; sales & marketing spend to remain flat in absolute terms but drive higher sales volume.
capex / expansion: No traditional capex; R&D primarily cloud-based with significant manpower and technical collaboration costs; no mention of hardware or infrastructure capex.
capital allocation: Zero debt; ₹200cr cash and cash equivalents; proposed dividend of ₹2.5/share; no buyback or M&A mentioned; focus on reinvestment in R&D and sales for enterprise growth.
risks & watch-items: Consumer segment decline may persist beyond Q2FY24; delayed renewals indicate weakening demand; enterprise product adoption may be slower than expected; competition from global players; reliance on distribution channels for consumer sales; regulatory uncertainty in data privacy space.
management quality / tone: Confident and strategic; acknowledges consumer headwinds as temporary; emphasizes long-term vision, R&D investment, and enterprise transition; highlights NIST collaboration as validation of technical credibility; optimistic about FY24 recovery.
non-obvious takeaways: NIST collaboration is not just PR — it grants access to U.S. government compliance frameworks and global B2B/B2G visibility, potentially unlocking international enterprise contracts; consumer decline is not due to market share loss but delayed renewals and reduced PC usage in micro-businesses, suggesting resilience in core customer base.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Quick Heal Technologies Limited is India's first listed cybersecurity company, developing indigenous security software for consumers under the Quick Heal brand and for enterprises and governments under Seqrite, with customers in more than 70 countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Quick Heal is a cybersecurity products and solutions company whose portfolio spans endpoint security, threat detection and response, zero trust access, data privacy, anti-fraud technologies and AI-powered security solutions. It sells to consumers, small businesses, government establishments and corporate houses, with the Seqrite brand serving the enterprise and government segments and the Quick Heal brand serving consumers. Products are built on in-house research at Seqrite Labs, described in the report as India's largest malware analysis facility, and on the GoDeep.AI behavioural-detection layer that runs across the enterprise and consumer suites.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Demand for privacy-led technologies and governance frameworks is expected to increase significantly as organisations prepare for evolving data protection requirements; management calls this a long-term structural opportunity for the industry
- Cybersecurity, privacy and compliance are converging into a unified business requirement, expanding the role of cybersecurity and creating new opportunities for value creation
- Government and international businesses continue to provide new growth opportunities while strengthening the diversity and resilience of revenue streams
- The consumer threat landscape has widened beyond malware to fraud, identity theft, phishing, social engineering and digital deception as digital payments, online banking and connected experiences grow
- The consumer business continues to face industry-wide challenges — management flags this explicitly while pointing to enterprise, innovation and next-generation technology investments as the offset
- India tailwinds: expansion of digital public infrastructure, rising internet penetration, widespread digital payment adoption and growing AI and cloud investment, supported by government initiatives on digital infrastructure, connectivity, AI, cybersecurity and data governance
- A cybersecurity maturity gap — industry studies indicate a large majority of Indian enterprises have deployed advanced security tools while overall cybersecurity maturity remains significantly lower, sustaining demand for readiness, governance and incident response
- Scale of threat telemetry as a product driver — more than 265 million detections across over 8 million endpoints during the year, averaging more than 500 detections every minute, feeding detection model development
- AI is a dual force: it accelerates defensive analysis and response while lowering the barrier for attackers, and management expects security operations to move from reactive monitoring towards intelligent, autonomous decision-making over the coming decade
- Regulatory baselines are tightening — GDPR and India's DPDP Act set strict new compliance requirements, and the Digital India Act would consolidate frameworks around cybersecurity prosecution, platform accountability and AI regulation
- Total income for FY 2025-26 declined 5.48% year on year on a consolidated basis; the Board's Report directs readers to the MD&A for the business outlook

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margins: >95% (unchanged YoY); total expenditure reduced by ₹12cr QoQ; R&D spend to be maintained at 25-30% of revenue; sales & marketing spend to remain flat in absolute terms but drive higher sales volume.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Zero debt; ₹200cr cash and cash equivalents; proposed dividend of ₹2.5/share; no buyback or M&A mentioned; focus on reinvestment in R&D and sales for enterprise growth.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Expansion during the year was capability-, footprint- and platform-led rather than plant-based; the report discloses no manufacturing capacity. Internationally, the company expanded its global footprint across SEA, MEA and LATAM, with a strategic partnership with Terrabyte extending reach across Southeast Asia and continued investment in Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Latin America supporting longer-term expansion. The enterprise portfolio was widened with newly launched Seqrite DRPS, Seqrite RRaaS and the AntiFraud.AI freemium version, while a partnership with the BHASHINI platform added AI capabilities in 22 languages and the Seqrite Data Privacy Management Platform secured its first enterprise customer. Institutional build-out included advanced cybersecurity laboratories being established with BIRD and NABARD to build cyber capabilities across rural and financial institutions. Internally, sales CRM, customer support, marketing automation and previously siloed IT applications were integrated into a unified digital ecosystem, new leadership was added across Engineering, People & Culture, Marketing, Delivery & Services and Channel & Alliances, and investment in R&D was deepened; a unified partner platform combining CRM, deal registration and customer support, plus structured credit cycles across the distribution network, was rolled out to the channel. On facilities, the R&D centre at Thube Park, Shivaji Nagar, Pune generated 6.81% of its total power requirement from a 45 kW solar plant, the seventh consecutive year of renewable generation there, and the Head Office and R&D centre in Pune and the Nashik office benefit from lower electricity tariffs and electricity duty exemptions under the Maharashtra IT Policy.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and strategic; acknowledges consumer headwinds as temporary; emphasizes long-term vision, R&D investment, and enterprise transition; highlights NIST collaboration as validation of technical credibility; optimistic about FY24 recovery.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Seqrite Labs, described as India's largest malware analysis facility, draws telemetry from over 8 million endpoints and recorded more than 265 million threat detections during the year, feeding detection intelligence into every product built on it
- GoDeep.AI acts as a single shared behavioural-detection intelligence layer across endpoints, networks and data environments, removing the need to run disparate detection engines
- Patent portfolio reached nine after two new Indian patents were granted during the year; patents cover signatureless behaviour-based detection, anti-ransomware and zero-trust access control
- Nearly three decades of R&D focused on computer and network security, with solutions indigenously developed in India
- Independent validation and institutional standing — collaboration with the NIST National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence on its Data Classification project, the AV-TEST Best Performance 2024 Award for Corporate Users for Seqrite Endpoint Protection, and recognition as a Gartner Preferred Vendor
- Service reach — 23 offices across 22 cities in India plus offices in the USA and UAE, supporting customers in more than 70 countries with over 900 cybersecurity professionals
- Certified operating base: ISO 9001:2015, ISO 20000-1:2018, ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type 2
- Partnership with the BHASHINI platform delivering AI capabilities in 22 languages, and with Terrabyte extending reach across Southeast Asia

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Consumer segment decline may persist beyond Q2FY24; delayed renewals indicate weakening demand; enterprise product adoption may be slower than expected; competition from global players; reliance on distribution channels for consumer sales; regulatory uncertainty in data privacy space.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: NIST collaboration is not just PR — it grants access to U.S. government compliance frameworks and global B2B/B2G visibility, potentially unlocking international enterprise contracts; consumer decline is not due to market share loss but delayed renewals and reduced PC usage in micro-businesses, suggesting resilience in core customer base.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen the enterprise cybersecurity business, winning and executing large, integrated cybersecurity engagements across enterprises, government organisations and critical sectors
- Expand the international footprint, with continued investment in Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Africa and Latin America to build global presence and new partner ecosystems
- Advance innovation across the cybersecurity portfolio, embedding AI to improve the speed, accuracy and effectiveness of threat detection and response through platforms such as GoDeep.AI and the Seqrite Intelligent Assistant
- Capitalise on …
